steps.note: The cheese is comminuted and mixed with water.
Phosphates such as disodium phosphate bind the cheese's calcium so the fat emulsifies, in a feed of 25–45 % dry matter.
The mix is held hot, in studies from 80 °C for 1–10 minutes to 85 °C for 45 seconds, and kept below 85 °C where possible to save volatile flavour.
The hot mix is passed through a sieve, and the undissolved cheese left behind.
It is usually homogenised in two stages, at about 150 and 50 bar, to make the emulsion stable.
It is spray-dried, often in two stages, a lab-scale dryer giving a soluble powder at 174 °C inlet and 68 °C outlet air.

links.name: Deshwal et al. (2024), A Review on the Production and Characteristics of Cheese Powders, Foods 13, 2204

sources.text: The steps of a cheese emulsion and its spray-drying and the ranges quoted from the studies the review lists; the review gives no single standard.
